verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. The repository states the display for an arbitrary family, not only for product-form fields. supported_cross_product_zero (LabelSumBounds.lean:523) takes two arbitrary families u, v of oscillations satisfying the predicate SupportedOscillations (:513): wherever a component is nonzero at (x, θ), the slow coordinate χ n x lies in closedWindow d (label) and Y n x lies in liftedSupport (nativeIndex …) (slotSet …). It concludes u l n (x,θ) i * v k n (x,θ) j = 0 for distinct labels, every θ and every pair of components. That is the display's implication with the hypothesis sets enlarged: closedWindow (:252) is a closed two-level, two-mesh-box window that contains the slow support (physicalMask_tsupport_closedWindow :308 states tsupport of the label mask lies in it), and slotSet is the closed rectangle of half-width 2r (orientedRectangle uses ≤), which contains the paper's open R^+_γ; liftedSupport is its preimage under cover^level. So the paper's hypothesis implies the Lean hypothesis by a stated inclusion and by unfolding definitions, and the paper's conclusion is the Lean conclusion with u = v. The Lean says more: the support sets in the hypothesis are larger, the two factors may come from different families, and the condition is pointwise non-vanishing rather than closed support. The window condition is on x alone for all θ, matching 'uniformly in θ'. Lean side conditions not printed in the display: band level ≥ 1 for both labels, x in an ambient set U, and 0 < q when passing from the mask support to the window. cross_product_zero (PartitionedCovariance.lean:323) and wave_cross_zero (:563) are product-form special cases proved separately; finding A saw only those, which is why it called the Lean weaker. Not verified term by term: that SlotColoring.Label, nativeIndex and cover are the paper's Γ, i(ℓ) and J_g, and that physicalMask's support is exactly K_γ of (6.9); I read their definitions and docstrings only.
